_encyclopedia.Western Heat Dome Mar 21 - Eastward Surg:
Western Heat Dome: 2026-03-21 -- Eastward Surge

What Happened
The heat dome began expanding eastward, pushing extreme anomalies into the Great Plains and challenging records in Texas, Oklahoma, and Nebraska. While the Western core remained dangerously hot, the eastward surge extended the event's footprint by hundreds of miles. WWA confirmed the 1-in-500-year classification.

Climate Attribution
Climate Shift Index: Level 5 (maximum). The WWA 1-in-500-year classification was confirmed. The event's magnitude and spatial extent are a product of anthropogenic warming. CSI 5 conditions now cover an area from the Pacific Coast to the Great Plains -- roughly 1,500 miles of continuous extreme anomaly.

Earth System Context
Climate Change: The eastward surge demonstrates how heat domes interact with the broader atmospheric circulation. As the ridge expands, it displaces the jet stream northward, pulling subtropical air into regions that normally experience cool spring conditions. The Great Plains in late March should be transitioning from winter -- instead, they are experiencing midsummer heat.

Freshwater Change: The expansion into Colorado and the Front Range intensifies the snowpack crisis. The Arkansas and Platte River headwaters are now in the anomaly zone. Municipal water systems in Denver, Colorado Springs, and downstream communities in Kansas and Nebraska depend on gradual spring melt -- not March flash-melt.

Biosphere Integrity: The Great Plains expansion brings the heat dome over the winter wheat belt. Winter wheat is vernalizing (completing its cold requirement) in March. Sudden heat can force premature heading, reducing grain fill time and yield. The US winter wheat crop, planted across Kansas, Oklahoma, and Texas, provides ~25% of US wheat production. Heat stress during vernalization is one of the highest-impact climate risks to global grain supply.

Land System Change: The expanded footprint means fire preconditioning now extends from California grasslands to Great Plains rangeland. Prescribed burn windows -- the controlled fires that reduce wildfire fuel loads -- are compressed or eliminated when conditions jump straight from winter to fire weather.

Record-Breaking Stations (as of 2026-03-21)
Phoenix AZ early: 95F (+17F) -- NWS issues first Extreme Heat Watch
Yuma AZ early: 98F (+16F) -- Already tracking 15+ above normal
Palm Springs CA: 96F (+16F) -- Coachella Valley heating up early
Las Vegas NV early: 92F (+22F) -- Heat dome compressing over Great Basin
Thermal CA: 100F (+18F) -- First triple digits in Salton Sea basin
Tucson AZ: 97F (+21F) -- Southern AZ corridor heating
Phoenix AZ record: 101F (+23F) -- Earliest 100+ day EVER recorded in Phoenix
Las Vegas NV record: 94F (+24F) -- Shatters all-time March high
Death Valley CA: 108F (+22F) -- Earliest 105+ in Death Valley
Yuma AZ record: 109F (+27F) -- Broke 1954 record of 108F
Martinez Lake AZ: 112F (+32F) -- Pending NWS validation - potential national record
Phoenix AZ peak: 105F (+27F) -- Earliest 105F on record
Denver CO: 85F (+30F) -- Heat bleeds into Rockies; snowpack crisis
Salt Lake City UT: 78F (+25F) -- Inland reach of heat dome
Albuquerque NM: 88F (+25F) -- Rio Grande corridor heating

Data & Sources
Temperature data: Preliminary synthetic grid seeded with confirmed NWS station records. ERA5 reanalysis expected ~April 2026.
Attribution: World Weather Attribution rapid analysis; Climate Central Climate Shift Index.
Planetary boundaries: Rockstrom et al. (2009), Richardson et al. (2023).
